key_insight: LoopWAM shows that robot policies can improve from real deployment rollouts, not just expert demos, by learning from the full spectrum of outcomes: successes, partial failures, and outright failures. Instead of discarding bad data or copying everything blindly, it uses closed-loop learning to turn interaction consequences into training signal.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the limitation of imitation learning where expert demonstrations alone are insufficient for generalist robot policies to improve in the real world. It addresses the challenge of using noisy deployment rollouts without reinforcing poor actions or losing useful physical feedback from failed attempts.
method: Introduces a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from deployment rollouts.
Uses rollouts from both the policy itself and other policies, covering successes, suboptimal behaviors, and failures.
Trains on the full quality spectrum of interactions so the model can learn from action consequences rather than filtering them away.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical path to continual improvement after deployment using real robot experience. It can reduce dependence on expensive expert relabeling and make generalist policies more adaptable in complex, real-world settings.

paper_title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
paper_authors: Wenxuan Guo, Yingping Liang, Zhaoguo Wang, Ziyuan Li, Angyuan Ma
